issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps/val_interval but code reads max_step and never uses val_interval
issues.detail: The docstring lists 'max_steps' and 'val_interval' as required keys, but __init__ reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular). Also val_interval is documented but never referenced; validation runs every save_interval steps instead. This is a data-shape bug: the contract between caller and trainer is inconsistent and will KeyError on the documented config shape. Pick one name, document it, and use it.

issues.description: specifier parsing uses split() on a space-delimited string, which collides with the documented colon-delimited format
issues.detail: args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() splits on whitespace, but the help text says specifiers are 'task:name:data_json[:factor]'. Multiple specifiers therefore must be space-separated, yet this is undocumented and there is no validation. Worse, the same code is not applied to train_unregistered_specifier, which is passed as a single string to DataIteratorFactory. The data flow is inconsistent: train takes one spec, valid takes many, but the CLI surface treats them identically. Fix the data shape: make the specifier list explicit (nargs='+' or a clearly delimited form) and apply uniformly.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint silently picks a stale checkpoint when resume_path is provided but does not exist
issues.detail: The logic is: if resume_path and resume_path.exists() -> use it; elif checkpoints dir exists -> use latest. If the user passes --resume_path pointing at a path that does not exist (typo, wrong mount), the code silently falls through to the latest checkpoint in output_dir, which is almost certainly not what the user wants. An explicit resume request should fail loudly, not be reinterpreted. The data structure (Optional[Path]) cannot distinguish 'no request' from 'request that failed', so the code conflates them.

issues.description: checkpoint sort by 'step_' substring split is fragile and will misorder on unrelated names
issues.detail: checkpoints = [d for d in ckpt_dir.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and 'step_' in d.name] then sorts by int(x.name.split('step_')[-1]). Any directory containing 'step_' anywhere in the name is included, and split('step_')[-1] picks the tail which may not be an integer (e.g. 'step_100_backup'), raising ValueError. The data shape is wrong: encode step as a structured name (e.g. exact prefix 'step_<int>') and parse with a regex, or store a manifest file. A small index file would replace this whole heuristic.

issues.description: valid() accumulates per-batch lists then averages without weighting by batch size
issues.detail: all_stats[key].append(value) then sum/len computes an unweighted mean of per-batch averages. If batches have different sizes (which they typically do with bucketed/length-batched loaders), this is biased. A correct shape is a running (sum, count) pair, or weight by batch size. This is a 'data dominates' problem: the wrong accumulator structure makes the bug invisible.

issues.description: run() saves a checkpoint every iteration of the outer while loop with no guard against re-saving the same step
issues.detail: After train() advances global_step by save_interval, run() saves; then valid() runs and another save fires next loop. If train() exits early (iterator exhausted before save_interval steps), global_step may not advance, and the loop saves the same step repeatedly and never terminates. There is no check that train() actually made progress, and no protection against duplicate checkpoint dirs. A small explicit state machine (or just 'if step did not advance, break') would make this obvious.

issues.description: freeze_param matching uses string startswith which over-matches sibling parameter names
issues.detail: The match is k.startswith(t + '.') or k == t. That is reasonable for module-path prefixes, but the iteration is O(params * patterns) for every init, and there is no warning if a pattern matched zero parameters. Silently-no-op freeze configs are a classic source of 'why is my fine-tune not converging' bugs. Either log the matched count per pattern, or assert > 0. The data structure should be 'set of frozen parameter names', built once, then checked.

issues.description: argparse uses inconsistent dash/underscore naming for closely related flags
issues.detail: --local_rank and --resume_path use underscores; everything else (--train-config, --output-dir, --train-unregistered-specifier, etc.) uses dashes. Argparse normalizes underscores in attribute names, but the CLI surface is inconsistent and surprising. Pick one convention. This is the kind of inconsistency Pike would strip in a five-minute pass.

issues.description: train_dtype is a method on the instance but takes ds_config as an argument and does not use self; should be a free function or staticmethod
issues.detail: train_dtype reads only ds_config and returns a dtype. It does not need self. Make it a module-level function (or @staticmethod) so the dependency is explicit and it can be tested without constructing a trainer. Small, but the data flow becomes obvious: ds_config -> dtype, a pure function, the simplest possible shape.

issues.description: valid_iterator_args is shared as a dict and passed via **kwargs; mutation risk and unclear ownership
issues.detail: valid_iterator_args is reused across two loops with **valid_iterator_args. If a future edit adds something to that dict mid-loop, behavior changes silently. Prefer named keyword arguments at the call site or a frozen dataclass. The data shape is a small ad-hoc dict that grows over time; promoting it to a typed struct (NamedTuple/dataclass) would make the contract with DataIteratorFactory explicit.

issues.description: wandb.config.update inside trainer __init__ couples trainer to global wandb state
issues.detail: The trainer asserts (in the docstring, not code) that wandb is already initialized, then writes wandb.config.update from inside __init__. This is hidden global state mutation. The docstring says 'will raise an error if wandb.run is None' but no such assert is present. Either add the assert (make the contract enforced, not just documented) or pass a logger object into the trainer and keep wandb out of it. A logger interface (log(name, value, step)) would let this trainer be tested without wandb at all.

issues.description: args.local_rank default is None but is passed directly to torch.cuda.set_device
issues.detail: If the launcher does not set --local_rank, set_device(None) will raise an opaque error. Default to int from env var LOCAL_RANK, or assert early with a clear message. Small, but it shows up as 'TypeError: an integer is required' in someone's logs at 3am.

review.summary: This is straightforward training-script code, and most of it is fine — the shapes are conventional (factory + trainer + DeepSpeed engine), and the loop is small. The real problems are in the contracts between pieces: trainer_args keys disagree with the docstring (max_step vs max_steps, val_interval documented but unused), the CLI specifier format mixes single-string and space-split-many-strings without explanation, and _load_checkpoint silently falls through to a stale checkpoint when an explicit --resume_path is wrong. Validation averaging is unweighted across batches, which is a classic 'wrong data structure' bug — a (sum, count) accumulator would make it obvious. The checkpoint discovery heuristic (substring 'step_' + split) should be replaced with a structured name or manifest. Strip the wandb coupling out of the trainer behind a tiny logger interface and this gets meaningfully smaller and more testable.
